title: prunella vulgaris subsp. hispida
intro: Prunella vulgaris subsp. hispida, commonly known as common selfheal, is a subspecies of the Prunella vulgaris plant, which is a low-growing, perennial herb native to Europe and Asia. It has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which can help to soothe skin irritations, reduce fever, and protect against infections. The therapeutic actions of Prunella vulgaris subsp. hispida include its ability to reduce inflammation, calm the nervous system, and promote wound healing, making it a popular ingredient in herbal remedies. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and volatile oils, which contribute to its medicinal properties and make it a valuable resource in natural medicine.
